title: upgrade attention kernels: FlashAttentionV2 + fused ops + rotary/ROPE optimizations
author: Priya Natarajan
description: Motivation: our current attention implementation (custom kernels + legacy flash attention) shows measurable tail latency and throughput regressions on long-context workloads and interacts poorly with continuous batching and KV cache hot paths. This PR upgrades attention kernels to a FlashAttentionV2-compatible path, adds fused attention/transpose ops used by the runtime to eliminate redundant memory copies, and fixes rotary/ROPE application edge-cases for mixed-precision and fused kernels. The change includes a new kernel selection flow that prefers fused ops when sequence length and dtype match optimized profiles, and falls back to safe paths otherwise. Key outcomes: reduced end-to-end p95 latency on long sequences, improved throughput for streaming/continuous-batching, and reduced per-token GPU memory bandwidth. Changes: 1) Add FlashAttentionV2 shim and kernel wrappers (crates/runtime/src/attention/flash_attention_v2.rs). 2) Implement fused attention + transpose ops (crates/runtime/src/attention/fused_ops.rs) to eliminate an extra reorder+copy in the runtime fast path. 3) Correct rotary/ROPE math in fused kernels and ensure consistent application order for cached KV reuse (crates/runtime/src/attention/rope.rs). 4) Kernel selection heuristics and schema for safe fallbacks (crates/runtime/src/attention/kernel_selector.rs). 5) Scheduler tweaks to prefer shorter-batch/low-latency queues for streaming requests to avoid blocking on large batching windows (crates/runtime/src/scheduler/mod.rs). 6) Add microbenchmarks and integration tests (tests/bench/kv_cache_bench.rs, pytests/test_attention_integration.py) and a rollout plan with gated canary and perf regression checks. Performance: in internal benchmarks on A100-80GB with mixed FP16/INT8 quantized models and a representative long-context chat workload (seq_len 4k, batch 1->8 continuous batching) we see ~12% reduction in p95 token latency, ~18% throughput improvement for sustained streaming workloads, and ~11% reduction in per-token memory bandwidth (detailed numbers in docs/perf/attention-kernels.md). Compatibility and safety: fused paths are opt-in via kernel selector flags and only enabled when the model dtype, rotary settings, and sequence-length thresholds match the vetted profiles. The PR includes correctness tests and an expanded integration matrix for mixed precision and KV cache warm/hot reuse. CI and validation: initial CI run surfaced a mismatch in ROPE parameter packing for cached KV; author updated kernel and added regression test; second CI run passed. Rollout: gated canary to 2% of traffic -> 10% -> 50% with automatic rollback on perf regressions or correctness alerts. Related: ENG-4291 (kernel performance initiative), SUP-1182 (customer incident showing p99 regressions with long contexts).
